questions.question: What is the central product invariant for generated code?
options: Every completion must be displayed, even after its deadline.
The assistant may propose code, but a developer or trusted workflow approves every durable change.
Repository retrieval may cross tenants when code is similar.
Generated tests may execute automatically in production.
questions.explanation: The assistant proposes rather than acts. Explicit approval keeps model output from becoming an unreviewed durable change.

questions.question: With 1 billion requests per day and a 4x peak factor, what peak request rate should the design approximately provision before extra headroom?
options: About 2,900 requests/s
About 11,600 requests/s
About 46,400 requests/s
About 4 million requests/s
questions.explanation: One billion divided by 86,400 is about 11,600 requests/s on average; multiplying by four gives about 46,400 requests/s.

questions.question: Repository retrieval is slow during an inline completion. Which degraded mode best preserves the design invariants?
options: Disable tenant checks to save time.
Retry retrieval indefinitely while the developer waits.
Use bounded cursor or file context, route to a compact model, or return no suggestion.
Send the whole repository directly to the model.
questions.explanation: Context and model capability may degrade, but authentication, tenant isolation, and safety controls remain mandatory.

questions.question: Why must every context query include both tenant and repository identity?
options: To make prompts longer and improve fluency.
To prevent cross-tenant or cross-repository retrieval from leaking private code.
To allow all customers to share one unrestricted cache.
To remove the need for authorization at the gateway.
questions.explanation: Identity-bound retrieval and cache keys enforce the privacy boundary throughout the context path.

questions.question: Which metric best exposes whether inference spending creates useful completion value?
options: Total accelerator utilization
Number of suggestions displayed
Cost per accepted character
Model parameter count
questions.explanation: Cost per accepted character links serving cost to useful developer action and exposes waste from stale or low-quality suggestions.

questions.question: A candidate improves acceptance but fails one cross-tenant retrieval test. What is the correct release decision?
options: Launch because aggregate acceptance improved.
Launch only to enterprise tenants.
Increase the model size and ignore the retrieval result.
Block release until the critical privacy failure is fixed and retested.
questions.explanation: Critical privacy and safety failures are hard gates; quality improvements cannot average them away.
